newsitem.title: USA: Actor Stallone slammed for buoys near Miami estate.
newsitem.headline: Actor Stallone slammed for buoys near Miami estate.

text.p: Actor Sylvester Stallone, who sparked a public outcry by setting up buoys to keep people away from his Miami estate, has agreed to move the buoys closer to shore, state officials said on Wednesday.
The actor recently circled the Biscayne Bay waters adjacent to his estate with several buoys that read "Keep out," saying his private dock had been approached by members of the public.
But Florida marine officials said the buoys violated the law. Stallone says he owns three acres of the bay at the bottom of his property, but they say the water is owned by the state.
The officials said that after public criticism, the actor agreed to move the buoys closer to shore and change the wording on them to "Shallow."

Stallone, a multi-millionaire best known for his roles in the "Rocky" and "Rambo" movies, has also been under fire in Miami lately for asking the city to build a gate to close off a popular pedestrian walkway near his mansion.
The buoy affair was settled one day before a city commission was due to meet on the gate issue, which has been dubbed "Stallonegate."
Paul Bloch, Stallone's Los Angeles-based spokesman, said the actor was not leading the effort to close the gate, but was merely the most high-profile advocate.
